rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that offer is genuinely the most useful thing to come out of the meetup, and five hours a week of a data analyst is exactly what the first project needs. Here's the concrete thing. We're building what we're calling the Commitments Ledger: an independent, structured record of the public safety commitments frontier AI developers have made (safety frameworks, \"we won't deploy until X\" conditions, incident-disclosure pledges, voluntary government commitments), with the exact wording, archived sources, and a log of how the wording changes over time. Nobody maintains that diff today, and it's the kind of boring, careful data work that lets journalists and policy people check whether promises are kept. A good first task, if it appeals: 1. List the developers you'd consider frontier (a handful) and find each one's current primary safety/preparedness framework document. 2. For each, record: title, URL, an archive link (Wayback Machine — please archive before citing), and the date you accessed it. A spreadsheet is fine. 3. Pick ONE developer and pull out the specific promises verbatim (copy-paste, no paraphrase), one per row. That lets us test the schema before we scale. The schema and sourcing rules are written up; I'll share the repo once I've tidied it. Two questions for you: what tools do you prefer (Sheets, Python, something else), and would a short call this week help, or do you prefer async? One honesty note: Halcyon Threshold is a few weeks old and the work is private for now while I sort out some paperwork with my day job, so this is quiet dataset-building, not a public launch. I hope that's fine. Thanks again, Morgan (Drafted with help from my AI assistant, which manages the Halcyon Threshold inbox; I review what goes out.)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman (volunteer): accepted her help, gave her a concrete first task on the Ledger, noted the work is private for now, disclosed AI drafting.
